text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam's new Criminal Code has been endorsed by the National Assembly. Under the new provisions people convicted of stealing public property worth more than $45,000 or of accepting a bribe worth more than $4,500 will automatically receive the death penalty or life imprisonment.
-- Vietnam and Thailand have agreed to start joint sea patrols in the Gulf of Thailand from October.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has approved plans for a tunnel under the Saigon River linking the central part of Ho Chi Minh City with city's northeast area.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has said security issues will be the biggest challenge for Asia in the 21st century.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has signed a decision to install a nationwide computer network to improve communications between state offices.
-- The National Assembly has agreed to extend its current session till May 10.
-- Vietnam has signed agreements with Thailand and Singapore providing for visa exemptions for people holding diplomatic and official passports.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for urgent reinforcement of measures to prevent deforestation.
-- The Government has issued a decree aimed at building a stronger military reserve force.
